explanation: This pole fires on the degree word that grades a health condition or health hazard: after a disease, pathogen or risk-factor subject (cancer, depression, S. aureus, smoking, physical inactivity) activation climbs through the copula and peaks on the determiner-plus-degree slot of the predicate ('a common', 'a severe', 'a major cause of', 'the third most common', 'one of the leading causes of'), and it peaks on the same degree words where they qualify a medical condition inside a noun phrase ('a common urologic complication', 'the leading cause of blindness', 'a significant cause of fatalities'). It sits at or below zero when those same degree words grade a benign or non-health topic ('a common practice', 'a common sight', 'a major source of renewable electricity', 'a major city', 'a major success') and when a health noun appears with no degree claim at all ('Cancer causes infection.', 'Cancer is treated with surgery.'), with the negative pole taking the benign side of the same axis (raw activation -5.6 on 'major' in 'a major source of renewable electricity').
